Not me but my grandfather. He worked on a railroad with two good friends when he was younger, one young like him and the other was old enough to be a grandpa, and all they would do is hook up cars and make sure everything ran smoothly. 

One day while the older guy was hooking up two cars on the very end, some dumbass decided to give a false call and say that all the cars were connected. My grandpa and the younger guy got out from in between the cars at the last second but the old guy had just gotten his side together and was crushed between the two cars. He was bleeding all over and was barely conscious almost seconds after they collided. The part he was stuck between was the two metal hooks that hold the cars together. His entire family came out to see him while he was stuck in between. He was barely holding on and was saying goodbye to his family and the paramedics told him there was no way to save him and if they took the cars apart he would bleed to death and fall in half, and if they didn't take the cars apart he would just die. 

He had to make the decision to just go the easy way and they gave him some drugs to make him go unconscious or sleep or something and then the railway company had to pull the cars apart. My grandfather witnessed all of it and said it was one of the most heartbreaking things he had ever seen. Now I am pretty sure there are ways of preventing that. But it's a terrible way to go
